major_issues: Mobile: the flow canvas is effectively unusable (content tiny and partially off-screen), with no obvious pan/zoom affordance beyond small +/- buttons; the main content becomes a dead area with low information density.
Mobile: header/status row wraps awkwardly (time drops to next line) and competes with primary title; hierarchy is unclear and wastes vertical space.
Right-side panel cards contain long strings (URLs, identifiers) that risk overflow/poor wrapping; readability suffers and lines look cramped.
Global contrast/readability: many secondary texts are too low-contrast on dark backgrounds (small gray labels, thin dividers), especially on mobile.
medium_issues: Inconsistent spacing/padding between card sections; some cards feel tight (metrics rows) while others have large internal gutters, reducing polish.
Discoverability: key controls (tabs, Fit, zoom +/- and refresh) are small and visually similar; active state is subtle and hard to scan quickly.
Composition: on desktop, the right rail is very dense while the left canvas has large unused dark space; balance feels off (either canvas should be larger or right rail should be collapsible).
Event strip at bottom of canvas is visually present but reads like a footer; its purpose/actions aren’t clear and it competes with other status surfaces.
minor_issues: Some labels use all-caps and small sizes which reduces legibility (e.g., section headers, pill labels).
Pill/chip components vary in padding/height; alignment within card content looks slightly uneven.
Shadow/glow effects are heavy; they reduce edge definition of cards and make the UI look a bit hazy rather than crisp.
The chevron on the Capital card suggests collapsible behavior but doesn’t clearly indicate expanded/collapsed state.

recommended_changes.change: Implement responsive layout rules: below ~900px switch to a single-column layout with the flow card becoming full-width and a fixed/min height (e.g., 60vh), and make the right-rail cards stack after it. Ensure the flow container uses overflow:hidden with clear internal scrolling/panning rather than shrinking content.

Add robust text overflow handling for long technical strings: apply `overflow-wrap:anywhere; word-break:break-word;` to card bodies, and for single-line chips/rows use `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; max-width:100%;` with optional title tooltip.

Increase baseline type sizes and contrast for secondary text on dark backgrounds (e.g., raise small labels to 12–13px on mobile, bump color from ~#7a7a7a to ~#a0a0a0, and strengthen dividers). Ensure WCAG-ish contrast for key labels/values.
Tighten and standardize spacing: set consistent card padding (e.g., 16px desktop / 14px mobile), consistent vertical gaps between sections (8–12px), and align chip heights/padding across the UI.

Rework header structure for mobile: keep 'Shadow Runtime' as primary, move host/status/time into a collapsible/secondary line with smaller type and controlled wrapping (e.g., a single-line marquee/ellipsis or two-line grid). Reduce vertical footprint above the fold.

Make controls more discoverable: increase hit targets for tabs/zoom buttons (min 40px), add clearer active tab styling (higher contrast underline/pill), and visually group zoom controls with a labeled 'Zoom' control cluster.

Improve mobile canvas interaction: add touch pan + pinch-zoom (or at least drag-to-pan) on the flow canvas; show a brief hint overlay ('Drag to pan, pinch to zoom') that dismisses after first interaction.
Reduce heavy glow/box-shadow and increase card border clarity (slightly brighter border + subtler shadow) to improve crispness and separation, especially on mobile.
Clarify accordion affordances (e.g., rotate chevron on expanded state) and ensure clickable rows have hover/focus states (keyboard-visible outlines) for polish/accessibility.

stop_reason: Not production-worthy yet due to mobile unusability of the primary flow visualization, weak header hierarchy/wrapping on small screens, and insufficient handling of long technical strings leading to readability/overflow risks.
